scenario: AI writes part of the scored essay during the same session.
expected_note: Joint human-AI performance; no independent-performance claim.

scenario: One hour later, students repeat the same items on paper under proctoring with AI prohibited.
Immediately after AI-supported practice, students solve new isomorphic problems without AI in a monitored lab.
Two weeks later, participants complete a novel task in a new context with device restrictions and logs.
expected_note: Delayed transfer evidence under documented non-use.

scenario: A paper reports a post-test but does not state whether AI was accessible.
expected_note: Do not infer AI removal from the word post-test.

scenario: AI is disabled for text generation but grammar correction remains available during the scored response.
expected_note: Report the exact restriction scope; not fully AI-free.

scenario: Participants use AI on Task 1 and perform a different creativity task without AI immediately afterward.
expected_note: Regime changes along multiple dimensions; not an isolated AI-removal effect.

scenario: A delayed test uses the identical questions from assisted practice.
expected_note: Delay supports persistence-related evidence but repetition limits transfer.

scenario: A survey asks whether participants feel they could perform without AI; no scored task is administered.
A coding assistant is available only for documentation lookup, not code generation, during a scored coding task.
expected_note: Availability must be scoped by construct-relevant AI function.

scenario: Participants complete an unassisted test one week later, but intervening AI use outside the study is not controlled.
expected_note: Assessment-time non-use can be documented even when intervening exposure remains a separate limitation.

scenario: The manuscript states 'independent exam' but provides no procedure describing tool access.
expected_note: Labels do not substitute for evidence of the assessment regime.
